title: To Live Is Christ
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Are you all in for Jesus? Not perfect, but decided. Don't live for the dot. Live for the line.
exhortation: I just love the attitude of this passage. It's one of my favorites because it focuses our purpose in this life. And it raises the question: what are we living for? Are we all in for Jesus? Can I say with Paul, "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain"?
By all in, I don't mean doing it perfectly. I mean you've decided to follow Christ 100 percent. You're no longer living for yourself, for money, fame or pleasure.

What does a life like that look like? It looks like joyful obedience and zeal for the church. It looks like calm resolve in the face of persecution, and wise decisions the world ridicules as foolishness. It looks like being ready to die. It looks like a radical life. It looks like being an honest salesman and a diligent employee when no one is watching, and a generous business owner. It looks like a godly dad who protects and provides for his family, and a godly mom who honors her husband and diligently teaches her children. It looks like the 21 Christians in Libya who were martyred for refusing to deny Christ, and Charlie Kirk, who was shot and killed after living a bold life defending the Christian faith. It looks like a youth pastor praying diligently for his students as he prepares to teach them, and like obeying God's call to be a pastor when you could make more money doing something else.

Randy Alcorn says this life is like a dot, and the next life is like a line going on into eternity. Don't live for the dot. Live for the line. So what is it for you? What is God calling you to do? I don't know the details, but God does. Go to him in prayer and ask him, and when he tells you, do it. Then we'll be able to say with Paul, "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain."
prayer: Lord, thank you that you have broken every chain. By your cross every sin is forgiven and every weight removed. Fill us with your Holy Spirit to live lives of holiness and righteousness in the power of the victory you have won.

Whoever we are and whatever we do today, as a mom, a dad, a salesman or a pastor, may we do it all for your glory and your kingdom, knowing who you are and what you have accomplished for us, and living in the victory you have won. Thank you, Jesus.
